q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-07#explanation: For almost a year American and British aircraft flew coal, food and medicine into West Berlin, until Stalin lifted the blockade in May 1949.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-08#question: Why is 1960 called the Year of Africa?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-08#choices.0: Because apartheid in South Africa came to an end
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-08#choices.1: Because the African Union was founded
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-08#choices.2: Because the Suez Canal was nationalized
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-08#explanation: Within a single year 17 states gained independence, among them almost all the French colonies as well as Nigeria, Somalia and the Congo.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-09#question: Which movement emerged from the Bandung Conference of 1955?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-09#choices.2: The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-09#explanation: At Bandung 29 Asian and African states called for a path of their own between the blocs; in 1961 they founded the Non-Aligned Movement in Belgrade.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-10#question: What did Rosa Parks do in 1955 to set off the Montgomery bus boycott?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-10#choices.0: She gave a speech before Congress
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-10#choices.1: She went on hunger strike in prison
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-10#choices.2: She refused to give up her seat to a white passenger
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-10#choices.3: She filed a lawsuit against the city of Montgomery
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-10#explanation: Parks remained seated on the bus and was arrested; the black population then boycotted the city's buses for 381 days.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-11#question: What does the policy of Deng Xiaoping from 1978 onward stand for?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-11#choices.2: For the break with the Soviet Union
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-11#choices.3: For reform and opening toward a market economy
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-11#explanation: Deng permitted private enterprise, created special economic zones and opened China to foreign capital, but held fast to the sole rule of the party.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-12#question: In which year did the Vietnam War end with the capture of Saigon by the North?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-12#explanation: The USA withdrew in 1973; on April 30, 1975 North Vietnamese troops took Saigon and united the country under communist rule.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-13#question: Who proclaimed the State of Israel in Tel Aviv on 14 May 1948?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-13#explanation: David Ben-Gurion read out the Declaration of Independence and became Israel's first prime minister. The first Arab-Israeli war began the very next day.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-14#question: What was the name of the first artificial satellite, launched by the Soviet Union in 1957?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-14#explanation: Sputnik 1 began orbiting the Earth on 4 October 1957. The resulting Sputnik shock drove the United States to invest heavily in space and education.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-15#question: Who became the first woman to fly into space in 1963?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-15#explanation: Soviet cosmonaut Valentina Tereshkova orbited the Earth for almost three days aboard Vostok 6 in June 1963. The first American woman in space, Sally Ride, followed only in 1983.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-16#question: Which US president declared "Ich bin ein Berliner" during his visit to West Berlin in 1963?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-16#explanation: Speaking outside Schöneberg Town Hall almost two years after the Wall was built, Kennedy assured the city of American solidarity. A few months later he was assassinated in Dallas.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-17#choices.0: A Soviet five-year plan for Eastern Europe
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-17#choices.1: A US aid programme for rebuilding Europe
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-17#choices.2: An agreement on the division of Berlin
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-17#explanation: Under the Marshall Plan, around 13 billion dollars flowed into Western Europe from 1948. The Soviet Union forbade the states in its sphere from taking part.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-18#question: Which doctrine declared in 1968 that the sovereignty of socialist states was limited?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-18#explanation: Moscow used the Brezhnev Doctrine to justify the invasion of Czechoslovakia in 1968. Only Gorbachev abandoned it in the late 1980s.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-19#question: Which politician led the Prague Spring in 1968?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-19#explanation: Communist Party leader Alexander Dubček sought "socialism with a human face". After the Warsaw Pact invasion in August 1968 he was removed from power.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-20#question: What happened in East Germany on 17 June 1953?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-20#choices.0: The founding of the National People's Army
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-20#choices.1: East Germany's accession to the Warsaw Pact
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-20#choices.2: A popular uprising that Soviet tanks crushed
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-20#choices.3: The closing of the inner-German border with a wall
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-20#explanation: What began as a strike by construction workers against higher work quotas turned into a nationwide uprising. In West Germany, 17 June was a public holiday until 1990.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-21#question: Who led the Polish trade union Solidarity?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-21#explanation: Electrician Lech Wałęsa led the 1980 strikes at the Gdańsk shipyard. He received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1983 and became President of Poland in 1990.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-22#question: Which West German chancellor knelt in 1970 before the memorial to the victims of the Warsaw Ghetto?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-22#explanation: The Warsaw genuflection became a symbol of reconciliation with Poland and of the new Ostpolitik. Brandt received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1971.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-23#question: Who was the first chancellor of the Federal Republic of Germany?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-23#explanation: Konrad Adenauer governed from 1949 to 1963 and firmly anchored West Germany in the West. Theodor Heuss had become the first federal president in the same year.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-24#question: Which treaties founded the European Economic Community in 1957?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-24#explanation: Six states signed the treaties establishing the EEC and Euratom in Rome on 25 March 1957. They built on the European Coal and Steel Community of 1951.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-25#question: Along which parallel was Korea divided before the Korean War?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-25#explanation: In 1945 the USA and the Soviet Union divided Korea into occupation zones at the 38th parallel. Vietnam, by contrast, was divided at the 17th parallel in 1954.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-26#question: In which battle did France decisively lose the war in Indochina in 1954?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-26#explanation: The defeat by Ho Chi Minh's Viet Minh ended French rule in Indochina. The Geneva Conference then provisionally divided Vietnam into North and South.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-27#question: Against which colonial power did Algeria fight its war of independence from 1954 to 1962?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-27#explanation: The Algerian War was one of the bloodiest wars of decolonisation and plunged France into a state crisis in 1958. The Évian Accords brought Algeria independence in 1962.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-28#question: Which country did Kwame Nkrumah lead to independence in 1957?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-28#explanation: The British Gold Coast became independent as Ghana in 1957, one of the first colonies in sub-Saharan Africa to do so. Nkrumah became a leading figure of Pan-Africanism.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-29#question: In which British colony did the Mau Mau movement fight in the 1950s?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-29#explanation: The British colonial power crushed the Mau Mau uprising with great harshness and internment camps. Kenya became independent in 1963, with Jomo Kenyatta as its first president.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-30#question: What triggered the Suez Crisis in 1956?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-30#choices.0: The closure of the canal by Israeli troops
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-30#choices.1: The construction of a rival canal by Saudi Arabia
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-30#choices.2: The sale of the canal to the Soviet Union
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-30#choices.3: The nationalisation of the Suez Canal by Egypt's President Nasser
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-30#explanation: When Britain, France and Israel then attacked Egypt, the USA and the Soviet Union forced them to withdraw. The crisis exposed the declining power of the old colonial empires.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-31#question: Which first prime minister of the independent Congo was murdered in early 1961?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-31#explanation: Lumumba had become head of government after independence from Belgium in 1960 and was caught up in the power struggles of the Congo Crisis. Mobutu established a dictatorship lasting decades in 1965.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-32#question: Who became the world's first female head of government in Ceylon, today's Sri Lanka, in 1960?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-32#explanation: Sirimavo Bandaranaike took over the government in 1960 after her husband's assassination. Indira Gandhi followed in India in 1966 and Golda Meir in Israel in 1969.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-33#question: What was the name of Mao Zedong's campaign from 1958 that caused a devastating famine?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-33#explanation: Mao wanted to industrialise China within a few years through people's communes and backyard steel furnaces. The resulting famine cost tens of millions of lives.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-34#question: In which country did the Khmer Rouge under Pol Pot establish a reign of terror from 1975 to 1979?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-34#explanation: The Khmer Rouge drove the urban population into the countryside; an estimated 1.5 to 2 million people died. Vietnamese troops ended the regime in 1979.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-35#question: Who became leader of the Islamic Republic of Iran in 1979 after the fall of the Shah?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-35#explanation: Khomeini returned from exile in France in February 1979 and turned Iran into a theocracy. After his death in 1989 he was succeeded by Ali Khamenei.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-36#question: In which war did Israel capture the West Bank, the Gaza Strip and the Golan Heights, among other areas, in 1967?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-36#explanation: In June 1967 Israel defeated Egypt, Jordan and Syria within a few days and also occupied East Jerusalem and the Sinai Peninsula. The occupied territories remain at the heart of the Middle East conflict today.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-37#question: Which Arab state was the first to sign a peace treaty with Israel, in 1979?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-37#explanation: After the Camp David negotiations of 1978, Anwar Sadat and Menachem Begin signed the treaty and Israel returned the Sinai. Jordan followed only in 1994.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-38#question: How did West Germany respond to the oil crisis at the end of 1973?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-38#choices.1: With ration cards for basic foods
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-38#choices.2: With a permanent speed limit of 80 km/h on motorways
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-38#explanation: On four Sundays in November and December 1973 private cars were banned from the roads, and people went for walks on the empty motorways. Oil prices had multiplied after the Yom Kippur War.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-39#question: With which country did West Germany sign its first agreement to recruit guest workers in 1955?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-39#explanation: The agreement with Italy was followed by Spain and Greece in 1960 and Turkey in 1961. Many guest workers stayed permanently and shaped Germany's immigrant society.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-40#question: In which year did women in Switzerland gain the right to vote at federal level?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-40#explanation: Only a referendum of male voters in February 1971 brought women's suffrage. The last canton, Appenzell Innerrhoden, had to introduce it in 1990 by order of the Federal Supreme Court.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-41#question: On what occasion did Martin Luther King give his "I Have a Dream" speech in 1963?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-41#choices.0: The march from Selma to Montgomery
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-41#explanation: In front of some 250,000 people at the Lincoln Memorial, King called for an end to segregation. The major civil rights and voting rights acts followed in 1964 and 1965.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-42#question: Which scientist provided a crucial basis for discovering the DNA double helix with her X-ray images?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-42#explanation: Franklin's famous "Photo 51" helped Watson and Crick design their model in 1953. She died in 1958 and did not live to see the Nobel Prize of 1962.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-43#question: Which disease did the World Health Organization declare eradicated in 1980?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-43#explanation: A worldwide WHO vaccination campaign defeated smallpox; the last natural case occurred in Somalia in 1977. It remains the only human disease ever eradicated.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-44#question: From which research network of the US Department of Defense did the Internet emerge?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-44#explanation: From 1969 the ARPANET initially connected four university computers in the USA. It was later switched to the TCP/IP protocol, which still forms the basis of the Internet today.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-45#question: Which pope, the first Pole in the office, strengthened resistance to communism in Eastern Europe from 1978?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-45#explanation: Karol Wojtyła was the first non-Italian pope in more than 450 years. His 1979 visit to Poland encouraged the opposition from which Solidarity soon emerged.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-46#question: In which present-day republic is the Chernobyl nuclear power plant located?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-46#explanation: On 26 April 1986 a reactor exploded there, and the radioactive cloud drifted over large parts of Europe. The Soviet leadership informed the public only days later.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-47#question: Which treaty settled the external aspects of German unification in 1990?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-47#explanation: The two German states and the four victorious powers signed it in Moscow on 12 September 1990. Germany gained full sovereignty and recognised the Oder-Neisse border.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-48#question: Which of these events happened first?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-48#choices.1: The founding of the Warsaw Pact
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-48#choices.2: The building of the Berlin Wall
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-48#explanation: NATO was founded in 1949, and the Warsaw Pact followed in 1955 as a rival alliance. The Wall was built in 1961, and the Cuban Missile Crisis came in 1962.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-49#question: What did Gorbachev and Reagan agree in the INF Treaty of 1987?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-49#choices.1: The withdrawal of Soviet troops from East Germany
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-49#choices.2: The elimination of all land-based intermediate-range missiles
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-49#choices.3: A ban on all nuclear weapons tests
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-49#explanation: For the first time an entire class of nuclear weapons was eliminated, including the Pershing II and SS-20 missiles stationed in Europe. Their destruction was verified by mutual on-site inspections.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-50#question: Which elected president did General Augusto Pinochet overthrow in Chile in 1973?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-50#explanation: The socialist Allende died in the presidential palace during the military coup on 11 September 1973. Pinochet ruled as a dictator until 1990.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-51#question: Which dictator did Fidel Castro and his guerrillas overthrow in Cuba in 1959?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-51#explanation: Batista fled Cuba on New Year's Eve 1958/59. Castro soon allied himself with the Soviet Union, which contributed to the Cuban Missile Crisis of 1962.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-52#question: What were students protesting against in the Soweto uprising of 1976?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-52#choices.1: Afrikaans as a compulsory language of instruction
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-52#choices.2: The closure of all mission schools
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-52#explanation: Police opened fire on the demonstrators on 16 June 1976; the photograph of the dying Hector Pieterson went around the world. The uprising became a turning point in the struggle against apartheid.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-53#question: Which politician made the term "Iron Curtain" world-famous in a speech in Fulton, USA, in 1946?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-53#explanation: Churchill said that an iron curtain had descended across Europe from Stettin to Trieste. The speech is regarded as an early signal of the Cold War.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-54#question: Which US president resigned in 1974 as a result of the Watergate scandal?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-54#explanation: Nixon's campaign team had arranged a break-in at the Democratic headquarters in the Watergate building, and he took part in the cover-up. He remains the only US president to have resigned.
q-lateinamerika-01#question: Which treaty divided the non-European world between Spain and Portugal in 1494?
q-lateinamerika-01#explanation: In the Treaty of Tordesillas of 1494 Spain and Portugal fixed a dividing line in the Atlantic; that is why Brazil fell to Portugal.
q-lateinamerika-02#question: Which woman interpreted for Hernán Cortés during the conquest of Mexico?
q-lateinamerika-02#choices.0: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz
q-lateinamerika-02#explanation: Malinche spoke Nahuatl and a Maya language and became indispensable to Cortés as interpreter and adviser.
q-lateinamerika-03#question: In which present-day country is the silver city of Potosí located?
q-lateinamerika-03#explanation: Potosí lies in the highlands of today's Bolivia, which at that time belonged to the Viceroyalty of Peru.
q-lateinamerika-04#question: Who defended the rights of the Indigenous peoples in the Valladolid debate of 1550/51?
q-lateinamerika-04#explanation: At Valladolid the Dominican Bartolomé de Las Casas argued against Juan Ginés de Sepúlveda for the human dignity of the Indigenous peoples.
q-lateinamerika-05#question: What was Palmares in the 17th century?
q-lateinamerika-05#choices.0: A silver mine in the Andes
q-lateinamerika-05#choices.1: A Jesuit reduction on the Paraná
q-lateinamerika-05#choices.2: The largest community of escaped enslaved people in Brazil
q-lateinamerika-05#choices.3: A port of the Manila galleon
q-lateinamerika-05#explanation: Palmares was a quilombo in north-eastern Brazil that held out against attacks for almost a century.
q-lateinamerika-06#question: Which Mexican nun defended the right of women to education in a famous text of 1691?
q-lateinamerika-06#choices.0: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz
q-lateinamerika-06#explanation: In her “Reply to Sor Filotea” Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz explained why women should be allowed to study.
q-lateinamerika-07#question: Which leader of an Indigenous uprising invoked the Incas and was executed in Cusco in 1781?
q-lateinamerika-07#explanation: José Gabriel Condorcanqui called himself Túpac Amaru II and led the great uprising in the Andes in 1780/81.
q-lateinamerika-08#question: Who declared the independence of Brazil in 1822 and became its first emperor?
q-lateinamerika-08#explanation: Crown Prince Pedro proclaimed independence on 7 September 1822 and became emperor as Pedro I.
q-lateinamerika-09#question: Which treaty ended the war between Mexico and the United States in 1848?
q-lateinamerika-09#explanation: In the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo of 1848 Mexico ceded California and other northern territories to the United States.
q-lateinamerika-10#question: To which Indigenous people did the Mexican president Benito Juárez belong?
q-lateinamerika-10#explanation: Juárez grew up in a Zapotec village in Oaxaca and only learned Spanish as a youth.
q-lateinamerika-11#question: Which states did Paraguay fight in the war of 1864 to 1870?
q-lateinamerika-11#explanation: Paraguay faced the Triple Alliance of Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay and lost a large part of its population.
q-lateinamerika-12#question: What is the name of the law with which Brazil completely abolished slavery in 1888?
q-lateinamerika-12#explanation: Princess Isabel signed the Lei Áurea on 13 May 1888; the earlier laws had only restricted slavery.
q-lateinamerika-13#question: Which Portuguese navigator reached the coast of Brazil in 1500?
q-lateinamerika-13#explanation: Cabral was actually bound for India but landed on April 22, 1500, on the coast of present-day Bahia and claimed the land for Portugal.
q-lateinamerika-14#question: Where does the name Brazil come from?
q-lateinamerika-14#choices.0: From the name of a Tupí chief
q-lateinamerika-14#choices.2: From the red brazilwood that was felled there
q-lateinamerika-14#choices.3: From the name of Cabral's flagship
q-lateinamerika-14#explanation: The red dyewood was the colony's most important trade good in its first decades and gave the country its name.
q-lateinamerika-15#question: Which Dominican friar accused the Spanish settlers on Hispaniola of mortal sin in an Advent sermon in 1511?
q-lateinamerika-15#explanation: Montesinos asked the settlers whether the Indigenous people were not human beings; in response King Ferdinand issued the Laws of Burgos in 1512.
q-lateinamerika-16#question: What was the encomienda in Spanish America?
q-lateinamerika-16#choices.0: A royal court that supervised the colonial administration
q-lateinamerika-16#choices.1: A Jesuit-run mission village for Indigenous people
q-lateinamerika-16#choices.2: An armed convoy of ships transporting silver
q-lateinamerika-16#choices.3: The assignment of Indigenous people to a Spaniard, to whom they owed tribute and labor
q-lateinamerika-16#explanation: In return the encomendero was supposed to protect the Indigenous people 'entrusted' to him and have them instructed in Christianity; in practice the system mostly amounted to exploitation.
q-lateinamerika-17#question: With which Indigenous people did Hernán Cortés ally himself against the Aztecs?
q-lateinamerika-17#explanation: Tlaxcala was an archenemy of the Aztecs; thousands of Tlaxcalan warriors fought alongside the Spaniards in the siege of Tenochtitlan in 1521.
q-lateinamerika-18#question: In which town did Francisco Pizarro capture the Inca ruler Atahualpa in 1532?
q-lateinamerika-18#explanation: At Cajamarca Pizarro lured Atahualpa into an ambush; he only founded Lima as a new capital in 1535.
q-lateinamerika-19#question: Who took office in Mexico City in 1535 as the first viceroy of New Spain?
q-lateinamerika-19#explanation: Charles V distrusted the power of the conquistadors and appointed Mendoza as his direct representative, who built up the administration, the tax system and a mint.
q-lateinamerika-20#question: What did the New Laws issued by Charles V in 1542 prohibit?
q-lateinamerika-20#choices.2: The export of silver to Asia
q-lateinamerika-20#explanation: Influenced by the reports of Las Casas, the Crown declared the Indigenous people free subjects; in Peru settlers under Gonzalo Pizarro rose in revolt in response.
q-lateinamerika-21#question: What was the mita in the Spanish colonial period?
q-lateinamerika-21#choices.0: A royal tax on the export of sugar
q-lateinamerika-21#choices.1: A town council of wealthy Creole citizens
q-lateinamerika-21#choices.2: A forced labor draft from Indigenous villages, for example for the mines of Potosí
q-lateinamerika-21#choices.3: A mission village run by Franciscans
q-lateinamerika-21#explanation: The Spaniards turned an old labor service of the Inca Empire into forced labor; many mita workers died from accidents, cold and mercury poisoning.
q-lateinamerika-22#question: Which substance was used in the amalgamation process to extract silver from crushed ore?
q-lateinamerika-22#explanation: The poisonous mercury came mainly from Huancavelica in Peru and Almadén in Spain; with this process silver output at Potosí rose sharply.
q-lateinamerika-23#question: Which two ports did the Manila galleon connect across the Pacific?
q-lateinamerika-23#explanation: The galleon sailed regularly from 1565 to 1815; in Manila Mexican silver was exchanged for Chinese silk and porcelain.
q-lateinamerika-24#question: What discovery set off a rush and a great wave of migration to Minas Gerais around 1695?
q-lateinamerika-24#explanation: Tens of thousands moved to new mining towns such as Vila Rica, today's Ouro Preto; as a result Brazil's capital was moved to Rio de Janeiro in 1763.
q-lateinamerika-25#question: For which Indigenous people did the Jesuits found the reductions in Paraguay from around 1609?
q-lateinamerika-25#explanation: At their height well over a hundred thousand Guaraní lived in some thirty reductions, protected from the encomienda and from slave hunters from São Paulo.
q-lateinamerika-26#question: Which Spanish king had the Jesuits expelled from all Spanish lands in 1767?
q-lateinamerika-26#explanation: The enlightened Bourbon ministers considered the order too powerful and too loyal to the pope; after the expulsion the Guaraní reductions fell into decline.
q-lateinamerika-27#question: Which woman, the wife of Túpac Amaru II, organized troops and supplies for the uprising of 1780?
q-lateinamerika-27#choices.3: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz
q-lateinamerika-27#explanation: Micaela Bastidas ran the rebels' headquarters and was executed in Cusco on May 18, 1781; Peru honors her as a heroine today.
q-lateinamerika-28#question: Which European power owned the colony of Saint-Domingue, which became Haiti in 1804?
q-lateinamerika-28#explanation: Thanks to sugar and coffee, Saint-Domingue was France's richest colony; half a million enslaved people worked there under brutal conditions.
q-lateinamerika-29#question: Who proclaimed the independence of Haiti on January 1, 1804?
q-lateinamerika-29#explanation: Toussaint Louverture had already died in French captivity in 1803; Dessalines gave the country the old Indigenous name Haiti.
q-lateinamerika-30#question: On what condition did France recognize Haiti's independence in 1825?
q-lateinamerika-30#choices.1: Haiti had to cede half of its territory
q-lateinamerika-30#choices.2: Haiti had to pay an indemnity of 150 million francs
q-lateinamerika-30#choices.3: Haiti had to accept the French king as head of state
q-lateinamerika-30#explanation: The payment burdened the country for more than a century; before that Haiti had been largely isolated by the slaveholding powers.
q-lateinamerika-31#question: Why did the Portuguese royal family move its seat to Brazil in 1808?
q-lateinamerika-31#choices.1: Lisbon had been destroyed by an earthquake
q-lateinamerika-31#choices.2: A revolution had proclaimed a republic
q-lateinamerika-31#choices.3: It wanted to prevent a slave revolt
q-lateinamerika-31#explanation: Under British escort the court reached Brazil; Rio de Janeiro gained a national library, a bank and a botanical garden, and in 1815 Brazil was raised to the status of a kingdom.
q-lateinamerika-32#question: In which city did Creole citizens depose the viceroy on May 25, 1810, and form a junta?
q-lateinamerika-32#explanation: The May Revolution was a response to Napoleon's occupation of Spain; in 1816 the United Provinces declared their independence at Tucumán.
q-lateinamerika-33#question: Which country did José de San Martín liberate after crossing the Andes in 1817?
q-lateinamerika-33#explanation: After the victory at Chacabuco, Bernardo O'Higgins took over the government of Chile; from there San Martín sailed on to Peru in 1820.
q-lateinamerika-34#question: Which present-day countries made up the republic of Gran Colombia founded by Simón Bolívar?
q-lateinamerika-34#explanation: After his victory at Boyacá in 1819 Bolívar founded Gran Colombia; his dream of a united South America, however, failed because of regional interests.
q-lateinamerika-35#question: Which battle sealed the end of Spanish rule in Peru in 1824?
q-lateinamerika-35#explanation: The independence forces won at Ayacucho in 1824; Chacabuco (1817), Maipú (1818) and Boyacá (1819) were earlier victories in Chile and Colombia.
q-lateinamerika-36#question: Which of these events happened first?
q-lateinamerika-36#choices.0: The May Revolution in Buenos Aires
q-lateinamerika-36#explanation: Haiti became independent in 1804; the May Revolution followed in 1810, Mexico's independence in 1821 and Brazil's in 1822.
q-lateinamerika-37#question: Which royalist officer switched sides, agreed to the Plan of Iguala and had himself crowned emperor of Mexico?
q-lateinamerika-37#explanation: Iturbide entered Mexico City with the army in 1821 but was overthrown as early as 1823; in 1824 Mexico adopted a republican constitution.
q-lateinamerika-38#question: Which people rose up in the Caste War on the Yucatán Peninsula in 1847 against land seizures and exploitation?
q-lateinamerika-38#explanation: The rebels held their own territory around Chan Santa Cruz for decades; the Mexican army only occupied it in 1901.
q-lateinamerika-39#question: What did the Mexican Liberals under Benito Juárez achieve with the Reform Laws?
q-lateinamerika-39#choices.1: The separation of church and state
q-lateinamerika-39#choices.2: The nationalization of the oil industry
q-lateinamerika-39#choices.3: The return of land to the Church
q-lateinamerika-39#explanation: The Church and communities also had to sell their landholdings; the dispute over this led to the Reform War of 1858 to 1861.
q-lateinamerika-40#question: Whom did Napoleon III install as emperor of Mexico in 1864?
q-lateinamerika-40#explanation: After the French troops withdrew, Maximilian was captured at Querétaro in 1867 and shot.
q-lateinamerika-41#question: Which country lost its access to the sea in the War of the Pacific (1879–1884)?
q-lateinamerika-41#explanation: Chile defeated Bolivia and Peru and won the nitrate-rich Atacama Desert; the loss of the coast still strains relations between Bolivia and Chile today.
q-lateinamerika-42#question: Where did most of the immigrants who went to Argentina between 1880 and 1914 come from?
q-lateinamerika-42#explanation: The millions of immigrants farmed the Pampas and made Buenos Aires one of the largest cities in the Americas, in whose port districts the tango was born.
q-lateinamerika-43#question: Where did José Martí found the Cuban Revolutionary Party in 1892?
q-lateinamerika-43#explanation: Martí lived in New York for about fifteen years and won over exiles and workers there for the uprising of 1895, in which he was killed as early as May 1895.
q-lateinamerika-44#question: From which state did Panama break away in 1903 with US support?
q-lateinamerika-44#explanation: Because Colombia rejected a canal treaty with the US, Washington backed Panama's independence and received the Canal Zone in return; the first ship passed through the canal in 1914.
q-lateinamerika-45#question: Against which long-time ruler was the 1910 uprising that set off the Mexican Revolution directed?
q-lateinamerika-45#explanation: Díaz had ruled almost continuously since 1876; Francisco Madero called for an uprising after his renewed reelection, and Díaz resigned in 1911.
q-lateinamerika-46#question: Who were called Creoles in Spanish America?
q-lateinamerika-46#choices.0: Descendants of Europeans born in the Americas
q-lateinamerika-46#choices.1: People of mixed European and Indigenous ancestry
q-lateinamerika-46#explanation: Creoles often owned land and mines but were passed over for high offices, an important reason for their leading role in the independence movement.
q-lateinamerika-47#question: What does the colonial principle 'I obey but do not carry out' describe?
q-lateinamerika-47#choices.0: Colonial authorities postponing unsuitable laws from Madrid
q-lateinamerika-47#choices.1: The conquistadors' oath of loyalty to the king
q-lateinamerika-47#choices.2: The obligation of Indigenous villages to perform labor service
q-lateinamerika-47#choices.3: The Jesuits' obedience to the pope
